label: try T49: the size of g_mom's within-type factors (dampings 0.75 and 1.0 against B0's 0.5) on the two counted E10.5 cuts; in both forms a labelled in-sample diagnostic: form A selects a constant on the cuts that kept g_mom, form B (M1 with R1, R2 and g_mom's factors) is the entry's form, whose one use is the veto; Feng's E9.5 cells lie inside these pseudo-tasks' external windows
limits: T49 chooses a value of one constant (B0's damping applied to g_mom) on the two cuts that kept g_mom and have read it seven times. Whatever it reads, it keeps nothing under rule 6, it is counted as tries, and its statement is a labelled in-sample diagnostic in both forms.

T47's 0.58 is a calibration of Feng's direction over M1's genes. It is not measured for g_mom's factors, whose zeroing removes most low-mean entries. g_mom's raw fit holds sampling noise, transport mismatch and the amplification of each state's own deviation as well as development (T23: about 40% of the gain with nothing developing; N21: R^2 0.35 to 0.64 from amplification). So a delivered share below 1 is expected of a noisy estimate and is not evidence that the size is too small. No outcome is read as 'g_mom was under-sized by a factor of about 3'.
Form B's veto reads the sign of an in-sample twin, and M1's step there is itself too small (T44). A veto or its absence says nothing about g_mom's size in the entry at test.

A larger arm redraws every count of every edited cell on a stream it does not share with its base, and its larger factors add resampling variance (about three times g_mom's at damping 1 on synthetic counts). Per-seed differences hold that noise, and a small part of any gain may be added spread rather than size.
'loses' is a sign on these cuts, not a size; 'not separated' includes steady gains below 0.3.
Run in the DGX checkout where T42 and T44 ran; a 1e-9 miss on b0, g_mom or m1_r_gmom voids the read uncounted and goes to the captain.

Twice the damping is not twice g_mom. It brings back the entries zeroed at 0.5, which are mostly sampling noise of low-mean genes, and grows the mean factor about fourfold over all entries; the clip does not bind. A larger arm's result is the result of that combined change and is not read as a size of the development g_mom measured.
One E8.5 -> E9.5 fit serves every seed and both cuts. The seeds measure draw and scoring noise only, n = 1 for the fit, and '8 of 10 ahead' is not replication.

The two cuts share their truth stage, reference and fit and are not independent evidence. Their truth differs from the reference in kind and depth (T27), and a gain from a larger spread may come from that difference rather than from development.
The order rule only makes the choice coarser. Any damping it names is chosen on these cuts and is a tuned constant, not a pre-registered one.
Form B's sign is in-sample and mixes g_mom's size with M1's step, which is itself too small on these cuts (T44). The veto can only hold back a form A result; it can never support one.

No outcome of T49 sets a damping at the test pair. There the fit crosses the change of sample kind and depth (T27, N21) that the E8.5 -> E9.5 fit does not, its leading direction does not carry from the backtest's fit (N21: |cos| 0.20 and 0.29), and a larger damping would enlarge a library contrast. A pass reads the size of the E8.5 -> E9.5 fit against an E10.5 truth only.

No value of T49's statement changes g_mom's damping in any entry or at test. A pass is a tuned in-sample size on cuts where 40% of g_mom's gain needs no development (T23). A veto or 'loses' is a sign on these cuts. 'Not separated' includes steady gains below 0.3. Each value goes to the captain with these sentences, and any change is the captain's ruling.

A gain at a larger damping fits three readings the read cannot tell apart: a faster pace on E9.5 -> E10.5 than on E8.5 -> E9.5, a scorer that rewards state-aligned spread or count noise, and the change of sample kind in the truth.
